I have farmed here in Ruvuma for over forty years. This quarter-acre plot is intercropped with beans and pigeon peas as we have always done. I will spread manure from my cattle before planting, use improved seed I kept from last season's harvest, and work the land with my wife and grandchildren—we do not buy chemical fertilizer or sprays for such a small home plot, and the rains here are usually enough without irrigation.
